name: Summary page polish: notes, sidebar, header menus

pr.title: Polish the summary page's notes, sidebar, and header
pr.head: a8cf3d521b8ec3d6b430e4b59fa2b7415473e92e

summary: A summary page is the guided review page that project summary publish puts on a repository's Projector site. Each file on the page is a card: a header, an optional one-line description, the notes about the file, and then its diff as one table per hunk. A note is a reviewer's remark, tagged context, verified, or concern. A note can sit under one line of the diff, at the top of a card about the whole file, or at the top of a section about several files. The sidebar on the left shows the pull request's stack, the projects it changes, the sections, and the published versions of the summary.

Notes under a line already render as rows of the diff table, with the tag in the line-number gutter and the text where the code starts. The other notes were bulleted lists, so their tags and text lined up with nothing in the diffs. This pull request makes the top notes on a card the same kind of row, in a small table that shares the diff's columns. A section's notes get the same layout as grid rows, with the tag in a column as wide as the diff's gutter. Every note on the page now starts its text at the same distance from the edge of its box.
It also reworks the sidebar, the headers, and the overview:

• A stack of one. The sidebar lists every pull request in a stack, one row each, with the current one highlighted. A pull request with no stack showed only its title in grey. It now shows the same list with one highlighted row. The build's data does not change: only the page draws the row.
  • Projects as rows. The projects a pull request changes were a line of links reading "Projects: …" below the stack. They are now rows above the stack, styled like the stack's but a step larger, at 13.5px with 9px of padding above and below, and the same 8px at the sides as a stack row, with each title spanning its row. Neither kind of row carries a tooltip repeating its title.
  • Credit and versions on the last row. The "Generated by Projector" credit moves from below the sidebar's box into the box's last row. A history icon at the right of that row opens the list of published versions below it. The icon's tooltip and accessible name read "Versions (N)", and the current version is marked with the secondary surface colour. With one version, the row holds only the credit.
  • Links behind a “…” menu. The page header's Conversation, Files, and Compare links, and each file's Diff, File, and Project links, move into menus that a “…” button opens. The items read Conversation on GitHub, Files on GitHub, and Compare on GitHub in the header, and View diff on GitHub, View file on GitHub, and View project on a file. Each menu is an HTML popover, which sits above the page and closes on Escape, on a click outside it, or when the page scrolls. A browser without popovers, such as Safari before 17, gets the links in place as a row under their short names instead.
  • File links follow the file. View file on GitHub opens the file on the head branch while the pull request is open, on the branch it merged into once it merges, which is the default branch unless it was a backport or a stacked layer, and at the head commit once it closes unmerged. Once GitHub reports the branch it merged into deleted, as merging a stacked parent usually does, the link moves to the default branch. A file the pull request deleted opens at the merge base, the last commit that has it. The site build now records the default branch on each page as defaultBranch, and the base branch GitHub reports as pr.currentBaseRef, null once that branch is deleted. The status query the build already runs fetches the base branch, so this adds no request.
  • Unlabelled Reviewed boxes. The section and file Reviewed checkboxes lose their visible “Reviewed” label. Each sits alone in a larger click target, with an accessible name such as “Mark src/app.py reviewed”.
  • Sidebar links. The sidebar's Overview and Files links share one line, sitting directly on the divider below them, and the divider that separated them from the stack above is gone.
  • More room in rows. Note rows get 13px of padding above and below their text instead of 5px, a file's one-line description gets the same 13px instead of 8px and is set at 15px, and the sidebar's stack rows get 8px on every side.
  • One checkbox size. Every checkbox on the page, for a section, a file, or a concern note, is 16px in the same green.
  • Notes, and no reading guide. A section's list of notes is headed Notes, not Review notes. The "How to read this" paragraph that every page appended to its "What this PR does" card is gone, so the card holds only what the summary wrote.
  • Collapsed files. A collapsed file shows only its header and description. Its notes on the whole file now hide with its diff.

cards.title: Review status at this head
cards.html:
• The first Projector review asked for one change: a line in docs/cli.md that the edit left unwrapped. The author rewrapped it, and later reviews found it fixed.
  • The reviews from 965ed38 to b57e5be were clean. Along the way, the author dropped notesList's unused class parameter and rewrote the pull request's description.
  • The review at 09fcf49 found that a browser without HTML popovers showed every “…” menu open. The author made the renderer draw the links in place there.
  • The review at 63e0fff found that a pull request merged into a branch other than the default linked its files on the default branch. The author made the link use the branch it merged into, and the re-review at 410306f found it fixed.
  • The author then closed the one case left open: a stacked layer merged into its parent's branch now links the default branch once GitHub reports the parent's branch deleted. The reviews at 7225ba0, f02368c, and this head are clean.
  • At this head the repository's gate passes: the site's type check and lint, the build (which reproduced the committed JavaScript exactly), all 514 unit tests, project check, and both plugin validations.
  • The sidebar rows dropped their title tooltips on purpose. A row's title is clamped to three lines, so a title longer than about 85 characters is cut, and the reader follows the link to read it in full.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Card: one file's block on the summary page, rendered by renderFile.
  • Top notes: the notes on a whole file, with no line. The code calls them loose.
  • Note row: a tr.noterow, with the tag in the gutter cell td.ngut and the text in td.nte.
  • Stack: the chain of pull requests whose bases are each other's heads. The build stores it as data.stack, empty for a pull request that stands alone.
  • Section notes: the notes on a whole section, drawn by notesList in a box headed Notes.
  • Popover: an element with the HTML popover attribute. The browser hides it until a button with a matching popovertarget opens it, then draws it above everything else on the page.

groups.title: The page renderer
groups.kicker: Notes line up with the diff's columns, the sidebar gets project rows, a one-row stack, and a shared last row, the headers' links move into “…” menus, and the file link follows the file.
intro: The summary renderer, site/src/summary.ts, builds the whole page in the browser from the summary's data. renderFile draws one card per file. Before this change it drew a note under a line as a table row inside the diff, and drew the top notes through notesList, the same bulleted list a section uses for its own notes.

Now renderFile has one function, noteRow, that turns any note into a table row. The diff's rows call it for notes under a line, and the top notes go through it into a separate table placed above the diff. That table gets the same class and the same <colgroup> as the diff's hunk tables, so its gutter is exactly as wide as theirs.

A section's notes stay a list, but each item is now a three-column grid: the tag, right-aligned in a 92px column, then the text, then a concern's checkbox. The diff's gutter is also 92px wide, two 46px columns or one 92px column, so a section's note text starts where a file's note text does. The Notes heading is inset 8px from the box's edge, as the diff's cells are from a file card's.

In the sidebar, projectsList draws the projects as a ul.stack.projects placed before the stack. renderPage moves the credit into the box, in a .navfoot row that also holds the versions toggle from headsList, and renderOverview no longer appends the reading guide. The stylesheet drops the rules for the old .prmeta line, the old .prtitle title, the versions chevron, the guide's .chip.inline chips, and the file links' .flink boxes.

The new moreMenu function builds a “…” button and its menu of links as an HTML popover, for the page header and for each file. wireSummary places each menu under its button, or above it where the window has no room below, and adds arrow-key movement between items, focus return to the button on close, and closing on scroll or resize. Where the browser has no popovers, moreMenu draws the links as a plain .morelinks row instead, and wireSummary has no menu to wire.

blobUrl picks the commit or branch for View file on GitHub. It reads the pull request's state and its current base branch, which the site build looks up on GitHub through pr_status in src/projector/summary.py, the base branch the summary recorded, and the new defaultBranch field, which the build in src/projector/site/__init__.py adds to each page.

checks.text: The compiled site/assets/summary.js is the TypeScript's build output and ships with the change. Rebuilding it at this head produced no difference.

files.note: Adds noteRow and the top-notes table in renderFile, reorders section notes, draws projects as sidebar rows, makes stackList fall back to a one-row stack, moves the credit and the versions icon into the box's last row, drops the reading guide, puts the header's and each file's links behind moreMenu popovers with an in-place fallback, makes blobUrl follow the file once the pull request merges, and drops the Reviewed checkboxes' visible labels.

checks.text: blobUrl links a deleted file at pr.base. A merged pull request's file links the base branch GitHub reports, or the recorded base when the build could not ask, then defaultBranch once that base is gone, then its head. A closed one's links its head, and an open one's its head branch. Tests cover a reported base, a retargeted base, a deleted base, a lookup with no base, and each state.

pr.currentBaseRef is absent when the build could not ask GitHub, so the recorded baseRef applies. It is null once GitHub reports the base branch deleted, so the link falls through to defaultBranch. A test covers each of those.

The renderer reads popover support once, as the page renders. Without it, moreMenu returns a .morelinks row with the same links, escaping, and new-tab rules, and no button or popover. A test renders the page both ways.

moreMenu escapes each href, label, and text. GitHub links open in a new tab with rel="noopener", and the project link opens in the same tab. The menu's id is pr-menu for the header and the file's id plus -menu for a file, so each id is unique.
A section's concern checkbox moves after the text. The checkbox handler still marks box.closest('li, tr'), so a checked concern dims its row. I traced it in the code.
A concern note's checkbox is keyed by the file's path, the same scope the top-notes list used at the base, so a concern a reader already checked stays checked. I traced it in the code.
The top table holds no tr.add, tr.del, or tr.ctx rows and no .src spans, so syntax highlighting and token marking, which read only those, leave it alone. I traced highlightFile and the token marker.
Each file's Diff, File, and Project links are now items in this menu, or the in-place row without popovers. Tests pin both, including that a file outside any project has no project link.
The checkbox keeps its file-box class and id, so the wiring that reads it is unchanged. Its accessible name escapes the path. A test checks both checkboxes and that no visible label remains.
The card ends after the summary's own paragraphs. A summary that relied on the page to explain the note kinds now has to say it in its overview.

stackList uses data.stack only when it lists two or more pull requests. Otherwise it draws one current row from the pull request itself. The current row returns before it reads url, so the empty url is never used. A test checks the rendered row.
Each project URL and title goes through esc, as the old .prmeta links did. The row has no title tooltip, so a title past the three-line clamp is cut.

.navfoot is positioned, so the versions toggle's absolute position is measured from this row and scrolls with the box. A closed details adds no height, since its list is its only in-flow content. A test checks this row with two versions and with one.

files.note: Styles section notes as gutter-aligned rows, lets the diff's note-row rules style the top notes, adds project rows, the last-row layout, the “…” menus, and their in-place fallback row, hides a collapsed file's notes, gives the Reviewed checkboxes larger targets and every checkbox one size, widens row padding, and drops unused rules.

checks.text: The window-height limit moves from .layout > .side to .side .nav, the box that now holds the credit. The site's own pages load this stylesheet, but their nav.side contains no .nav element, so this rule does not reach them. I checked the markup in site/src/site.ts.
This rule outranks the shared row rule, so only project rows take the larger type. Project and stack rows share 8px of side padding, so a project title starts where a stack row's number does.

This rule is more specific than .prblock > :first-child, which zeroes the first child's top margin, so it wins. It applies only when the projects list leads the block, which renderPage always does when there are projects. The first project title then sits about 19px below the box's top border and 20px in from its left, as the comment says.
The label around each Reviewed checkbox stays the click target, now a 34px square for a section and a 28px one for a file, outlined on hover.

One rule sizes and colours the section, file, and concern-note checkboxes. The rules that place a concern's box, .notes li .nbox and table.diff td.nte .nbox, are more specific, so they still set its margin. Only checkbox inputs carry nbox, which I checked in the renderer.
The new rules select .notes li. The file header's note badge is a span.badge.notes with no list items, so these rules leave it alone.
A closed popover is hidden only by the browser's own popover rule. A browser without popovers never gets this markup, because the renderer draws a .morelinks row there instead.
A file that starts collapsed, such as a test or a document, hides its whole-file notes until the reader expands it. The note badge in its header still counts a concern that is unchecked.
This padding applies to every note row in a diff, both under a line and at the top of a card.

files.note: Types the page data's new pr.base, pr.currentBaseRef, and defaultBranch fields.
The site build adds defaultBranch to every summary page, and pr.currentBaseRef when the status lookup answered.

checks.text: trunk is always a string here: it defaults to main, and build_site passes the default branch it was given, or else the checked-out branch.
The key is set only when the lookup returned base, so a page built without asking GitHub has no currentBaseRef, and the renderer falls back to the recorded base branch.

files.note: The pull request status query also asks for the base branch, and pr_status returns its name as base, or None once the branch is deleted.

checks.text: This field rides on the query the build already runs for each pull request's state and reviews, so it adds no request.

groups.title: Tests and documentation
groups.kicker: Node-rendered tests cover the new markup, and the CLI reference and the summary format name the new menu items.
intro: FileHeaderTests in tests/test_site.py builds a summary and renders it with the compiled script under node. Tests check the markup of a whole-file note and a section note, the one-row stack, the project rows before the stack, the versions icon and the shared last row, an overview card that holds only the summary's text, both “…” menus with their links, the in-place links where a browser has no popovers, the file link for each pull request state, for a merge into another branch, for a base branch GitHub retargeted or deleted, and for a deleted file, and the Reviewed checkboxes' accessible names. They skip when node is missing. SummarySidebarTests reads the stylesheet and checks where the window-height limit and the scroll now sit. PrStatusTests in tests/test_summary.py checks that the status query asks for the base branch and that a deleted one reads as None.

docs/cli.md describes the site's sidebar and file cards. It says that a pull request with no stack is a stack of one, names the “…” menus and their items, and gives the rule for View file on GitHub. skills/summarize-pr/format.md, the summary format a summary's author follows, gives the same rule, and now says a reader marks a file reviewed with the checkbox in its header.

checks.text: The expected markup pins the exact column group: two lncol columns for a file with both sides.
